# Myth — Genealogy, Transformation, and Technē

Myth carries an argument by giving its forces bodies, desires, consequences, and memory. *The Return of Zero* uses a small number of mythemes repeatedly, allowing each one to change as the essay crosses from logical relation into psyche, technology, and governance. The history therefore begins with what the ancient texts actually narrate and follows what later thinkers and the essay make those scenes capable of showing.

## Aphrodite, Ares, Harmonia

[Hesiod's *Theogony*](../../../sources/classical-philology/hesiod/hesiod-1920-theogony-evelyn-white/hesiod-1920-theogony-evelyn-white.md) provides the genealogy. The selected passages identify Cytherea with Aphrodite and place Harmonia among the children born to Aphrodite and Ares, alongside Panic and Fear. The poem gives a family relation, not a theory of reconciliation. That restraint makes the image stronger in [§2 · #3](../../../../../section-rooms/03-two-logics/movements/22-s2-p3-ares-aphrodite-harmonia.md): the essay's reading begins from a genuine genealogy and asks what it means that war and love can bear both terror and concord.

Harmonia becomes the name for a third form produced by retained tension. Ares carries separation, contest, and expenditure; Aphrodite carries attraction, value, and generative meeting. Their relation has no guaranteed happy synthesis. Panic and Fear remain in the same genealogy. Concord names one possible fruit of a dangerous conjunction. [Heraclitus B51](../../../sources/classical-philology/mackenzie/mackenzie-2021-heraclitean-allusion-odyssey/mackenzie-2021-heraclitean-allusion-odyssey.md) belongs beside it because the fragment makes differing and agreement one backwards-turning fastening, embodied by bow and lyre.

The mytheme returns in [§4 · #2](../../../../../section-rooms/05-psychoid-flowering/movements/33-s4-p2-complexio-quaternity-senarius.md), where Jungian *complexio oppositorum* gives psychic form to the same demand. Conscious and unconscious positions do not disappear into a compromise; their energetic relation can produce a capacity that neither held alone. By then the history has moved from genealogy, through logic and music, into individuation.

## Hephaestus and the bonds

[Book VIII of the *Odyssey* in Murray's translation](../../../sources/classical-philology/homer/homer-1919-odyssey-murray/homer-1919-odyssey-murray.md) supplies the other scene. Hephaestus's cunning bonds immobilise Ares and Aphrodite; he summons the gods to witness; shame and unquenchable laughter complete the public exposure. The source says “bonds,” and the narrative concerns capture, complaint, spectacle, and release. The essay's technological reading grows from those actions.

Hephaestus builds an apparatus to secure a relation that no apparatus can make reciprocal. The bonds produce observability and proof while replacing encounter with enclosure. The episode's own vocabulary carries the anatomy: Helios keeps a σκοπιή, a lookout (8.302); the bonds forged "fine as spiders' webs" are δεσμοὶ τεχνήεντες, artful bonds, technē written on the device (8.279–81, 296–97); the gods are convened to *see* (ἴδησθε, 8.306–7); "unquenchable laughter" pays out the spectacle (8.326) while the goddesses withdraw in αἰδώς (8.324); and the wrong is priced in a coined word, μοιχάγρια, the adulterer's fine (8.332), alongside the demand for the ἕεδνα back. The scene ends in what Greek law recognises as formal surety: Poseidon, the god who does not laugh, pledges — and finally in his own person, "I will myself pay thee" (8.355–56) — what the trap could never extract, and the bonds open. Philosophy of technology later found its exact word for the shape of this device: Heidegger's *Ge-stell*, the gathering (as *Gebirg* gathers mountains) "which gathers man thither to order the self-revealing as standing-reserve" — a gathering that arrests, which the essay names the counterfeit gathering and sets against both Indra's recursive net and the *legein* of Heraclitus B50, "the Laying that gathers." No prior scholarship connects the Homeric episode to enframing; the pairing is the essay's own move, made with its warrants shown.

The scholarly control sits close by. Burkert's 1960 study hears Demodocus's song as the victory of technē over physis — "the slow catches the swift… by his arts" (τέχνῃσι, 8.329–32) — a philological classic already reading the episode as a verdict on craft-intelligence against violent strength. Brown reads the scene through real Greek practices of public shaming and the exposure of adulterers; Phillips reads it as ideal aetiology of adultery law, the surety exchange included; Detienne and Vernant place circle, net, and bond at the centre of *mētis*, Hephaestus's crooked feet its "visible symbol." In [§2 · #3](../../../../../section-rooms/03-two-logics/movements/22-s2-p3-ares-aphrodite-harmonia.md), all of this becomes the felt difference between relation and containment. In [§5 · #3](../../../../../section-rooms/06-objective-internality/movements/40-s5-p3-preference-hidden-zero.md), the same image tests preference and evaluation systems: a field becomes Hephaestian when its owner, protocol, or audience can expose and rank participants from a position they cannot contest — and the surety closure adds the deeper criterion, that observability alone concludes nothing, since even the perfected trap had to borrow a person's pledge to end its own scene. In [§5→0 · #3](../../../../../section-rooms/07-instrument-returns/movements/46-s50-p3-4-2-mono-poly.md), the net becomes a governance test for the sovereign commons. Provenance and legibility serve relation only when agency and return remain possible.

## Apollo and Dionysus

[Nietzsche's *Birth of Tragedy*](../../../sources/phenomenology-continental-philosophy/nietzsche/nietzsche-1910-birth-tragedy-haussmann/nietzsche-1910-birth-tragedy-haussmann.md) is the historical hinge between Greek divine figures and modern psychology of culture. Nietzsche frames art through Apollonian and Dionysian powers whose conflict receives periodic reconciliation, then describes tragedy as their reciprocal linguistic union. Apollo brings image, boundary, measure, and dream; Dionysus brings participation, dissolution, music, and intoxicated unity. Nietzsche's formulation already resists the flat opposition into which the pair is often reduced.

[§2 · #4](../../../../../section-rooms/03-two-logics/movements/23-s2-p4-complex-dynamism.md) uses the pair to protect the two logics from their corresponding failures. Form without participatory depth petrifies; participation without form dissolves the distinctions relation needs. [§4 · #4](../../../../../section-rooms/05-psychoid-flowering/movements/35-s4-p4-gebser-apollo-dionysus.md) carries the history through Gebser: integral consciousness makes each structure transparent to the origin and co-presence of the others. Apollo and Dionysus become mutually diaphanous rather than reconciled by a superior third term.

## Prometheus, Atlas, and the technological imagination

[Jorjani's *Prometheus and Atlas*](../../../sources/media-technology-philosophy/jorjani/jorjani-2016-prometheus-atlas/jorjani-2016-prometheus-atlas.md) belongs to the modern philosophy of technology, where mythic figures gather questions of foresight, power, burden, and world-building. It extends the historical field in which technē remains inseparable from the image of what human making is for. The Antikythera mechanism then gives this mythic imagination a recovered material body in [§5→0 · #2](../../../../../section-rooms/07-instrument-returns/movements/45-s50-p2-antikythera-attunement.md): craft coordinates celestial cycles for a finite observer.

## Indra's net through Huayan

The philosophical jewel net used here reaches the essay through Chinese Huayan Buddhism. Its divine name and cosmic scale draw upon the Indian figure of Indra, while its precise recursive operation is carried by the [Dushun-attributed *Huayan wujiao zhiguan* passage](../../../sources/indian-philosophy/dushun/dushun-cleary-2000-jewel-net-indra/dushun-cleary-2000-jewel-net-indra.md), preserved at T45, no. 1867, 513a28–513b21 and selected here in Thomas Cleary's translation, “The Jewel Net of Indra.” Every jewel reflects the others; those reflections contain further reflections; a local point opens repeatedly into the net that constitutes it. The source house keeps the attribution qualified and withholds exact English quotation until Cleary's printed pages 58–60 have been collated.

[Van Norden and Jones's Huayan account](../../../sources/indian-philosophy/van-norden/van-norden-jones-2024-huayan-sep/van-norden-jones-2024-huayan-sep.md) supplies the doctrinal and historical control. They associate the metaphor with the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* and explain its Huayan force through dependence in existence and identity, recursive reflection, and mutual inclusion without loss of distinctness. That final condition matters: interpenetration relates determinate members; it does not dissolve them into an indistinct mass.

The essay's opposed-net reading begins from this recovered operation. In [§0 · #3](../../../../../section-rooms/01-differentiating-mind/movements/10-s0-p3-apoha.md), the jewel net images a determination constituted through a field it does not own. In [§2 · #3](../../../../../section-rooms/03-two-logics/movements/22-s2-p3-ares-aphrodite-harmonia.md), Indra's recursive reflections meet Hephaestus's Homeric bonds: one scene intensifies relation through every member, while the other immobilises its members for an external witness. [§5→0 · #3](../../../../../section-rooms/07-instrument-returns/movements/46-s50-p3-4-2-mono-poly.md) develops that difference as a governance test. The Huayan sources establish the affirmative net; the `0/1` reading and its confrontation with Hephaestus belong to the essay's mythematical development.
